classification.difficultyReason: Match each component to the square or rectangle key, including rotated rectangles, then express the counted areas as multiples of m and n.

content.prompt: In each of the following, the area of the square shown in the key is $m\text{ cm}^2$ and the area of the rectangle shown in the key is $n\text{ cm}^2$. Give the area of each shaded region in terms of $m$ and $n$.

spec.description: Square area key, retained with the shared instruction.
spec.mathematics: One square has area m square centimetres.

spec.description: Upright rectangle area key, retained with the shared instruction.
spec.mathematics: One rectangle has area n square centimetres; it is longer than it is wide.

spec.description: Three squares in a horizontal row between two upright rectangles. All tops align; rectangles extend below the squares. Internal boundaries remain visible.
spec.mathematics: Three square pieces and two rectangle pieces, with disjoint interiors.
spec.answerVisibility: No answer or piece counts printed.

answer.worked:
There are 3 squares and 2 rectangles.

$$\begin{align*}A&=m+m+m+n+n\\A&=(3m+2n)\text{ cm}^2.\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Four squares form a two-by-two block. One horizontal rectangle is centred above it and another below it.
spec.mathematics: Four square pieces and two rotated rectangle pieces, with disjoint interiors.
spec.answerVisibility: No answer or piece counts printed.

answer.worked:
There are 4 squares and 2 rectangles.

$$\begin{align*}A&=m+m+m+m+n+n\\A&=(4m+2n)\text{ cm}^2.\end{align*}$$
